exact_signatures.statement:
{E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E] [SecondCountableTopology E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E} [ProbabilityTheory.IsGaussian μ]
    {L : ℝ≥0} {f : E → ℝ} (hf : LipschitzWith L f) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable f μ ∧ ∀ t : ℝ,
      MeasureTheory.Integrable
        (fun x => Real.exp (t * (f x - ∫ z, f z ∂μ))) μ

{E S : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    [MeasurableSpace S] {V : E → ℝ} {κ : ℝ}
    (hκ : 1 ≤ κ) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E, κ⁻¹*‖v‖^2 ≤ fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v v ∧
      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v v ≤ ‖v‖^2)
    {eta : S → ℝ} {y : S → E} (heta : Measurable eta) (hy : Measurable y)
    (hpos : ∀ s, 0 < eta s) :
    let F := fun s x => V x + (eta s)⁻¹/2*‖x-y s‖^2
    ∃ p : S → E, Measurable p ∧
      (∀ s, p s + eta s • gradient V (p s) = y s) ∧
      (∀ s z, F s (p s) + (κ⁻¹+(eta s)⁻¹)/2*‖z-p s‖^2 ≤ F s z ∧
        (F s z ≤ F s (p s) ↔ z=p s)) ∧
      (∀ s t, eta s = eta t → ‖p s-p t‖ ≤ ‖y s-y t‖) ∧
      let G := fun q : S × E => gradient V (p q.1+Real.sqrt (eta q.1) • q.2)
      Measurable G ∧
      (∀ s t z w, eta s = eta t →
        ‖G (s,z)-G (t,w)‖ ≤ ‖y s-y t‖+Real.sqrt (eta s)*‖z-w‖) ∧
      ∃ K : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel S E, ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel K ∧
        (∀ s, K s = (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E).map (fun z => G (s,z))) ∧
        ∀ s, MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun w : E => w) (K s) ∧
          ∀ (a : E) (t : ℝ), MeasureTheory.Integrable
            (fun w => Real.exp (t * inner ℝ a (w - ∫ v, v ∂K s))) (K s)

canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.NormedAddCommGroup E: additive commutative group with norm and compatible metric; no probability, moment, gradient or concentration certificate
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.NormedSpace ℝ E: real vector-space scalar multiplication compatible with norm; generic leaf Banach carrier
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.InnerProductSpace ℝ E: positive-definite real inner product inducing norm; finite Euclidean presentation
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.CompleteSpace E: metric Cauchy completeness; no integrability certificate
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.SecondCountableTopology E: countable topology base; generic separable Banach/Borel setting
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.FiniteDimensional ℝ E: Module.Finite ℝ E, finite spanning set; dimension zero is allowed
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.MeasurableSpace E/S: sigma algebra structure; S is arbitrary parameter carrier
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.BorelSpace E: measurable_eq: sigma algebra equals borel E
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.ProbabilityTheory.IsGaussian μ: map_eq_gaussianReal: for every continuous linear form L, μ.map L=gaussianReal (∫L dμ) (Var[L;μ]).toNNReal. Gaussian probability follows from zero linear form; no IsProbabilityMeasure binder is added. Supports noncentered and degenerate Gaussian laws.
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.LipschitzWith L f: ∀x y, edist(f x)(f y)≤L*edist(x)(y), finite L:NNReal; genuine mathematical leaf premise
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.Integrable f μ: AEStronglyMeasurable f μ AND HasFiniteIntegral f μ; genuine absolute first moment, not a totalized integral identity
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.Kernel S E: toFun:S→Measure E plus measurable measure-valued map; output object, no supplied selector
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.stdGaussian E: literal product of gaussianReal 0 1 over Fin(finrank E), mapped by orthonormal basis synthesis; canonical identity covariance finite Gaussian probability
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.gradient V: Riesz inverse of fderiv V; totalized to zero only off differentiability, which hV:C² excludes everywhere
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v v: second Frechet derivative evaluated twice in v; C² assures genuine derivative everywhere, Hessian quadratic form
canonical_class_and_definition_expansion.prox p: existential output characterized by stationarity, strong growth and iff unique minimizer; no choice/fallback definition supplied

objects.evidence: G(s,z)=gradient V(p(s)+sqrt(eta(s))•z), K(s)=stdGaussian.map G_s; p genuinely characterized unique minimizer; generic leaf f scalar Lipschitz.

domains.evidence: Source R^d represented finite Hilbert E; generic leaf is complete second-countable Banach Gaussian, broader canonical infrastructure; every positive eta valid for domain finiteness.

quantifiers.evidence: ∃single measurable p and K, then ∀s actual vector integrability and ∀a∈E ∀t∈ℝ integrability. No nonzero/unit/a-sign/t-sign restriction.

assumptions.evidence: C² and exact normalized Hessian source standing assumptions retained. Family measurability is representation-level. Generic hf must be constructed from Hessian/oracle internally. IsGaussian internally implies probability.

conclusion.evidence: First Bochner moment is Integrable id (K s), and exponential is centered by ∫id d(K s). It is not centered at smoothed gradient and states no sharp inequality.

scopes_senses.evidence: Ordinary absolute/L1 and all real signed exponential domains. No proof, compiler, semantic decoder, publication or whole Lemma4.2 completion approved.

edge_case_review.dimension_zero: Source consumer G,p,y are unique zero vector, K Dirac0, first moment0 and exp1. Generic zero-domain leaf f is a constant real, first moment finite and centered exponent0.

edge_case_review.allpositive_eta: No upper eta bound mathematically needed for moment/domain; source numerical query regime η≤1/(2β) and adjacent smoothed-Hessian lemma η≤1 stay explicitly excluded. Allpositive producer cannot certify numerical work regime.

independent_mathematical_justification: Lipschitz growth |f(x)|≤|f(0)|+L‖x‖ and Gaussian first norm moment give genuine first moment; Gaussian squared-norm exponential integrability with small positive parameter implies exp(c‖x‖) integrability for every finite c by Young inequality. Every signed centered directional exponential is dominated by a finite constant times that radial exponential. Actual vector first moment follows from vector Lipschitz linear growth on finite-dimensional E. These are reviewed mathematical routes, not checked Lean proofs.
